question: In maternal health, what does 'morbidity' mean?

options.A: The death of a woman while pregnant or within forty-two days of delivery
options.B: The total number of pregnant women admitted to a tertiary hospital
options.C: Any infection contracted by a newborn baby during the first week of life
options.D: Any health condition caused or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth

explanation: Think of morbidity simply as the illnesses, injuries, or health struggles that happen because of pregnancy—distinct from maternal mortality, which means death. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h1)

question: Which of these makes a urinary tract infection automatically classified as 'complicated'?

options.A: The patient is a non-pregnant adult female
options.B: The infection occurs in a male patient
options.C: Urinalysis shows trace amounts of blood
options.D: Symptoms started less than 24 hours ago

explanation: Because of male anatomy and possible prostate involvement, any UTI in a male is automatically treated as complicated. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h5)

question: Why are anticholinergic drugs sometimes given to patients right before surgery?

options.A: To reduce oral and respiratory secretions
options.B: To lower the patient's blood pressure
options.C: To completely paralyze skeletal muscles
options.D: To induce deep general anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Drying up spit and mucus helps keep the airway clear and stops fluid from getting into the lungs during surgery. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which vital sign check needs immediate nursing action after a patient takes a sedative?

options.A: Respiratory rate dropping below twelve breaths per minute
options.B: Oral temperature measuring 37 degrees Celsius
options.C: Heart rate staying steady at seventy-two beats per minute
options.D: Blood pressure reading of 120 over 80 millimeters of mercury

explanation: A slow breathing rate is a major red flag for dangerous central nervous system depression. Always watch the airway first! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

options.A: To legally sign medical documents on behalf of busy attending physicians
options.B: To order hospital kitchen meals based on patient dietary preferences
options.C: To schedule nursing shift rotations and manage monthly hospital payrolls
options.D: To provide automated prompts and guidelines that assist clinicians in making safe choices

explanation: You got it! CDSS software acts like a smart assistant, analyzing patient data to give helpful alerts and evidence-based tips. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why do hospitals still rely on high-temperature incineration for certain waste, despite environmental concerns?

options.A: It is the only method permitted for ordinary kitchen food leftovers
options.B: It transforms dangerous clinical trash into reusable office furniture
options.C: It requires zero financial investment to build and maintain
options.D: It completely destroys difficult pathological waste and reduces overall volume

explanation: Some body tissues and heavy clinical waste need intense heat to completely and permanently wipe out disease risks. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: Which room setup is most important when getting ready for a physical exam?

options.A: Bright flashing lights for visibility
options.B: A cold room temperature to prevent sweating
options.C: Adequate privacy and good lighting
options.D: Open doors to encourage fresh airflow

explanation: Good lighting helps you see subtle skin changes clearly, and privacy helps your patient relax and feel secure with you. Always set the stage for comfort! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h2)

question: What happens in the condition known as vasa praevia?

options.A: When the placenta implants directly over the lower uterine segment
options.B: When fetal blood vessels run across or near the internal cervical os
options.C: When the placenta peels away from the uterine wall prematurely
options.D: When severe inflammation of the cervix causes heavy spotting

explanation: Vasa praevia occurs when unprotected fetal blood vessels cross the cervical opening ahead of the baby, putting the fetus at extreme risk if they rupture. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of milieu therapy on a psychiatric ward?

options.A: Creating a safe and therapeutic environment for recovery
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital building maintenance
options.C: Isolating disruptive patients from the general public
options.D: Testing new experimental pharmaceutical products

explanation: Milieu therapy uses the physical layout and daily social interactions on the ward to create a secure, structured space where healing can happen. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is cancer staging so important after a patient receives a confirmed diagnosis?

options.A: It guides treatment decisions and helps determine the overall prognosis
options.B: It identifies the exact environmental toxin that caused the disease
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will achieve full remission
options.D: It completely replaces the need for any laboratory blood tests

explanation: You got it! Staging lets the team know how far the cancer has spread, which helps them choose the best treatment plan and understand what lies ahead. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T3#GNS321_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is it so important to report an accidental needle-stick or blood exposure immediately?

options.A: Post-exposure preventative treatments work best when started quickly
options.B: Agency managers need time to discipline the careless worker
options.C: Insurance companies will refuse claims filed after twenty-four hours
options.D: State laws make late reporting a criminal offense for nurses

explanation: Time matters! Preventive medicines for bloodborne infections like HIV or Hepatitis B work best when taken very soon after an exposure. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h8)

question: Why are Environmental Health Officers so important to the primary healthcare team?

options.A: They handle all financial audits for the local health authority
options.B: They prescribe medications for chronic non-communicable diseases
options.C: They prevent disease by managing water, sanitation, and hygiene
options.D: They substitute for nurses during severe staff shortages

explanation: They tackle the root causes of sickness by making sure water sources are clean, surroundings are sanitary, and hygiene practices are up to standard. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of advance directives in long-term care?

options.A: To outline a resident's treatment preferences before they lose decision-making capacity
options.B: To schedule mandatory physical therapy sessions for new admissions
options.C: To determine the monthly financial billing rates for facility room and board
options.D: To assign nursing shift schedules for the upcoming week

explanation: Spot on! Advance directives let people speak for themselves ahead of time about the medical care they want if they ever become unable to decide. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T2#GNS324_U5_T2_h7)

question: How does poor rural road infrastructure negatively impact healthcare delivery in Nigeria?

options.A: It automatically lowers the birth rate in urban centers
options.B: It causes nurses to abandon their profession entirely
options.C: It delays emergency medical referrals from primary clinics to tertiary hospitals
options.D: It prevents international organizations from sending financial reports

explanation: Bad roads and difficult transport make moving critical emergency cases, such as obstructed labor or severe trauma, extremely slow and dangerous. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: A patient with cancer is losing weight fast despite eating regular meals. What is a good first step to help them?

options.A: Reduce total daily protein intake to spare the kidneys
options.B: Initiate a strict low residue diet
options.C: Limit fluid intake during meal times
options.D: Switch to a high calorie, energy-dense meal plan

explanation: When the body's metabolic needs shoot up, boosting the energy density of food helps the patient stop losing weight and regain strength. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h2)

question: What is the main goal of Family Life Education?

options.A: Surgical treatment of reproductive organ diseases
options.B: Preventative learning and healthy relationship development
options.C: Psychiatric medication management for depression
options.D: Emergency trauma care for injured children

explanation: Spot on! Family Life Education is all about teaching healthy habits and preventing issues before they start, rather than treating illnesses or emergencies. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a health promotion program?

options.A: To increase the cost of purchasing imported drugs
options.B: To check if the program achieved its goals and used resources effectively
options.C: To prove that the government needs no further assistance
options.D: To find reasons to dismiss junior healthcare staff

explanation: Evaluation helps determine what worked well, what failed, and how future health interventions can be improved. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)

question: Which patient condition means Oral Rehydration Therapy is unsafe, requiring IV fluids instead?

options.A: Mild watery diarrhea with normal skin turgor
options.B: Profound hypovolemic shock with altered consciousness
options.C: Low-grade fever and mild nausea
options.D: Frequent loose stools without vomiting

explanation: If a patient is in shock or unconscious, they cannot swallow safely. They need quick intravenous fluids to restore their blood pressure. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h6)

question: Why is localized swelling and extra blood flow actually a good thing when you have an infection?

options.A: It prevents any fluid from entering the damaged tissue spaces
options.B: It stops all cellular activity so the body can rest completely
options.C: It lowers local body temperature to kill heat-sensitive viruses
options.D: It brings white blood cells quickly to the site to fight invaders

explanation: Swelling and extra blood flow aren't just uncomfortable; they are high-speed delivery routes rushing white blood cells straight to the battlefield to clear out germs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h5)

question: How do indirect causes of maternal morbidity differ from direct causes?

options.A: They are pre-existing medical conditions made worse by pregnancy
options.B: They have no effect on the overall health of the unborn baby
options.C: They only occur during the third trimester of pregnancy
options.D: They are entirely caused by surgical mistakes during delivery

explanation: Indirect causes are health issues the woman already had—like heart disease or severe malaria—that flare up because the body is working extra hard during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h4)

question: What is the main goal of giving Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) to someone with HIV?

options.A: To replace damaged CD4 cells with donor bone marrow
options.B: To suppress viral replication to undetectable levels
options.C: To cure opportunistic infections without antibiotics
options.D: To completely eradicate the virus from every body cell

explanation: ART stops the virus from multiplying, keeping viral counts super low and protecting the immune system. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h7)

question: Why are strong drugs like norepinephrine given through a central line instead of a regular vein in the hand or arm?

options.A: To avoid the need for any blood pressure monitoring equipment
options.B: To reduce the total cost of nursing care during the shift
options.C: To prevent severe local tissue damage if the medication leaks out
options.D: To speed up how fast the drug reaches the brain and heart

explanation: These medications can cause severe skin and tissue damage if they leak outside a small peripheral vein. Central lines are much safer for them! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h3)

question: When we classify joints by their 'function', what are we actually looking at?

options.A: The presence of a fluid-filled cavity
options.B: The type of tissue binding the bones
options.C: How much movement the joint allows
options.D: The specific shape of the bone ends

explanation: Great thinking! Functional classification simply looks at how much motion a joint gives you—whether it moves a lot, a little, or not at all. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T6#GNS121_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why is enteral tube feeding preferred over parenteral nutrition when the digestive tract works?

options.A: It delivers pure water without any dissolved nutrients
options.B: It requires no monitoring of blood glucose levels
options.C: It preserves gut function and protects the intestinal lining
options.D: It carries zero risk of infection or mechanical blockage

explanation: Using the gastrointestinal tract keeps the gut mucosa healthy and prevents bacterial translocation, making enteral feeding the safer choice. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h7)

question: A community health nurse finds three new cases of tuberculosis in a neighborhood. What is the best immediate step for managing the human reservoir?

options.A: Spraying chemical disinfectants on local streets and pathways
options.B: Tracing and screening close contacts of the infected individuals
options.C: Ordering all residents in the town to stay indoors for a month
options.D: Vaccinating all stray dogs and cats living near the neighborhood

explanation: Contact tracing lets us find other people who might be carrying the germ without knowing it yet, so they can get checked and treated early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h3)

question: A nurse researcher has finished reviewing literature and picking out variables. What should they do next?

options.A: Destroy all notes taken during the literature search
options.B: Submit the final budget to the finance office
options.C: Select a mapping approach to connect the variables
options.D: Discharge all patients currently in the ward

explanation: Once you have your key variables written down, the fun part starts: figuring out how to draw the lines and boxes to connect them! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h5)

question: What is a common misunderstanding about the role of the triage nurse?

options.A: That triage nurses are responsible for performing major surgical procedures
options.B: That the triage nurse works exclusively in the hospital pharmacy
options.C: That it is merely a clerical desk job rather than a high-level clinical assessment
options.D: That triage staff never interact directly with incoming patients

explanation: Triage is real clinical nursing! It takes sharp assessment skills and quick thinking to spot hidden dangers at the front desk. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main job of the body's immune system when it comes to body tissues?

options.A: To destroy the body's own healthy cells
options.B: To distinguish between self and non-self
options.C: To produce energy for cellular repair
options.D: To circulate red blood cells through tissue

explanation: Spot on! The immune system's core superpower is knowing the difference between what belongs to your body (self) and foreign invaders (non-self). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h1)

question: When does a pregnant woman's blood pressure usually drop to its lowest point?

options.A: During the second trimester
options.B: Right before active labour begins
options.C: During the first few weeks postpartum
options.D: Immediately after delivery

explanation: You got it! Vascular resistance drops around mid-pregnancy, bringing blood pressure down before it goes back up near term. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h4)

question: Why do heart muscle cells packed with so many mitochondria?

options.A: To store excess calcium ions required for action potential plateaus
options.B: To manufacture contractile proteins like actin and myosin on demand
options.C: To continuously produce large amounts of ATP needed for constant pumping
options.D: To regulate the body's overall systemic blood pressure levels

explanation: Your heart never takes a break! It needs a massive, non-stop supply of ATP power plants (mitochondria) to keep beating 24/7. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T10#GNS121_U3_T10_h5)

question: Why do some parasite eggs cause long-term, painful inflammation in body tissues?

options.A: They cause immediate chemical burns on the skin surface.
options.B: They get trapped in organs and trigger immune system reactions.
options.C: They rapidly convert human muscle tissue into adult worms.
options.D: They release large amounts of pure oxygen into the blood cells.

explanation: When eggs get stuck in organs like the liver, the body fights back by forming tiny nodules called granulomas. Well reasoned! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why is quarantine used as a public health tool during an outbreak?

options.A: To stop exposed people from spreading the disease further
options.B: To cure people who already have the infection
options.C: To punish individuals who travel without permission
options.D: To test new vaccines on healthy populations

explanation: Restricting movement of exposed persons prevents them from passing germs to the community during the incubation period. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h1)

question: What three things does the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) check?

options.A: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.B: Heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure
options.C: Reflex strength, coordination, and balance
options.D: Pupil reaction, temperature, and skin color

explanation: You've got this! GCS is a quick way to grade brain function by checking if the patient opens their eyes, talks, and moves. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is considered a direct cost of a physical disability?

options.A: Losing daily wages while resting
options.B: Missing a promotion due to bias
options.C: Reduced workplace productivity
options.D: Buying a wheelchair and mobility braces

explanation: Direct costs are the actual out-of-pocket prices you pay for items specifically needed because of the impairment, like assistive devices and drugs. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h3)

question: What patient position is standard and most appropriate for inserting a rectal suppository?

options.A: Upright sitting position in a chair
options.B: Prone position lying flat on the stomach
options.C: Sims position on the left side
options.D: Flat on the back with legs held high

explanation: The Sims position naturally aligns with the downward curve of the sigmoid colon and rectum, making insertion easier. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h7)

question: What common side effects of metronidazole should you warn your patient about so they don't panic?

options.A: Permanent yellowing of the skin and eyes
options.B: Complete loss of the sense of smell
options.C: Metallic taste and dark-colored urine
options.D: Sudden swelling of the hands and feet

explanation: A metal taste in the mouth and darker urine can look scary to a patient, but it's totally normal with metronidazole. Giving a quick heads-up saves them a lot of worry! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which substance requires a nursing mother to wait patiently until it clears her bloodstream before breastfeeding again?

options.A: Alcohol
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Water
options.D: Garlic

explanation: Alcohol passes straight into breast milk and clears out only as it leaves the mother's bloodstream. Timing and caution are key here! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h6)

question: Why is early physical therapy encouraged soon after amputation surgery?

options.A: To stretch the skin until it breaks open for drainage
options.B: To force the brain to stop feeling the missing limb
options.C: To prevent joint stiffness and maintain muscle strength
options.D: To prevent the patient from ever needing a wheelchair

explanation: Getting moving early keeps the joints flexible and stops the muscles from getting weak before it's time for a prosthesis. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h6)

question: Who benefits the most when a community achieves herd immunity?

options.A: Patients recovering from surgical procedures
options.B: Only individuals with strong innate immunity
options.C: Vulnerable people who cannot receive vaccines
options.D: Only adults who travel to other countries

explanation: Spot on! Herd immunity builds a protective ring around fragile individuals who cannot take vaccines themselves. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h6)

question: What is one of the biggest roadblocks to successful quality improvement in a clinical unit?

options.A: Excessive availability of hospital funding
options.B: Too much free time for bedside staff
options.C: Having too many willing volunteers
options.D: Fear of blame and lack of a safety culture

explanation: That's right! When nurses are scared of being punished for speaking up, mistakes stay hidden under the rug, and the unit can't learn or improve. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h6)

question: How can bedside nurses directly help with hospital financial efficiency?

options.A: By collecting taxes from patients at the hospital gate
options.B: By preventing waste of medical supplies and reducing patient complications
options.C: By negotiating insurance premium rates directly with corporate bosses
options.D: By deciding the annual national health budget in Parliament

explanation: As a nurse, being careful with consumables and preventing infections (like bedsores) means patients heal faster and use fewer resources—saving everyone money! [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a warning sign of a pelvic infection after a procedure?

options.A: Foul-smelling or purulent vaginal discharge
options.B: Severe and worsening lower abdominal pain
options.C: Persistent fever and chills
options.D: Sudden development of normal morning appetite

explanation: Spot on! Wanting to eat normally is a sign of a happy, healing body. Fever, bad-smelling discharge, and terrible pain are the real warning signs to watch out for. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h8)

question: Why do nurses always encourage families to eat a variety of different foods?

options.A: Diversity in meals prevents food from spoiling in storage.
options.B: Eating only one type of food is the cheapest way to survive.
options.C: Eating a wide variety of foods ensures the body gets a complete range of essential nutrients.
options.D: Eating different foods eliminates the need for clean drinking water.

explanation: Brilliant! No single food item has every nutrient our bodies need, which is why a mixed diet is the secret to good health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four key elements needed to prove malpractice?

options.A: Guilt
options.B: Damages
options.C: Duty
options.D: Breach

explanation: To prove malpractice, you need duty, breach, causation, and damages. 'Guilt' belongs in criminal law, not civil malpractice cases. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h3)

question: What is the main goal of managing an injured victim while they are inside a moving ambulance?

options.A: To complete all surgical procedures before hospital arrival
options.B: To prevent further injury and keep vital organs working
options.C: To diagnose the exact cause of the accident during transit
options.D: To discharge the patient home if vital signs stabilize

explanation: The transit phase focuses purely on stabilizing critical functions and protecting the patient from additional harm until they reach definitive care. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which of these best describes an environmental reservoir for a disease germ?

options.A: A mosquito biting a person with malaria
options.B: An asymptomatic person carrying typhoid
options.C: A nurse caring for an infected child
options.D: Soil containing tetanus spores

explanation: Soil, water, and air can act as environmental reservoirs where germs live naturally outside of a human body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h5)

question: What is an empyema?

options.A: A collapsed section of lung from mucus
options.B: A blood clot traveling from the leg to the lungs
options.C: A pocket of pus collected in the pleural space
options.D: A permanent stretching of the main breathing tubes

explanation: An empyema happens when a lung infection spreads into the space around the lungs, forming a pocket of pus that usually needs to be drained. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h8)

question: Which of these common grains naturally contains gluten?

options.A: Sorghum
options.B: Rice
options.C: Millet
options.D: Barley

explanation: Barley is one of the main grains that naturally contains gluten, along with wheat and rye. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h1)

question: Why is promoting homestead gardening a useful nursing strategy against distribution failures?

options.A: It guarantees that families will never need to buy water or soil
options.B: It completely replaces the need for community health clinics
options.C: It reduces a household's total reliance on fragile transport supply chains
options.D: It stops commercial farmers from growing cash crops for export

explanation: Growing food locally around the home provides an independent, reliable source of nutrition when transport systems break down. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h8)

question: What is the most common and versatile suturing technique used for simple emergency lacerations?

options.A: Retention bridge stitch
options.B: Simple interrupted suture
options.C: Subcuticular continuous stitch
options.D: Continuous running lock

explanation: Simple interrupted stitches are quick to place and provide reliable closure where each stitch stands alone. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why does a nurse monitor the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) for a patient receiving heparin?

options.A: To measure the exact number of active platelets in the bloodstream
options.B: To check if the patient has developed an iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To ensure the intrinsic and common pathways are appropriately suppressed
options.D: To evaluate how well the liver is producing new red blood cells

explanation: Heparin affects the intrinsic pathway, so checking the aPTT lets the nurse know if the drug dose is safe and effective. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to start a health program without doing a situation analysis first?

options.A: Community members will refuse to ever speak to healthcare workers
options.B: The government will refuse to disburse salaries to the nursing staff
options.C: Local pharmacy shops will immediately report the clinic to the police
options.D: The program might target problems the community does not consider important

explanation: Skipping situation analysis often leads to wasted resources because interventions fail to address the actual priorities of the local population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses mix cytotoxic drugs inside special safety cabinets?

options.A: To keep the sterile medication free from room dust
options.B: To warm the liquid solution before intravenous infusion
options.C: To speed up the chemical dissolution of the powder
options.D: To prevent accidental exposure from drug splashes or aerosols

explanation: Spot on! These cabinets protect you from breathing in tiny invisible droplets or getting splashes on your skin while mixing. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h4)

question: What is one of the biggest duties of a community health nurse when dealing with NCDs?

options.A: Manufacturing affordable insulin and blood pressure drugs in local clinics
options.B: Performing major neurosurgeries in rural primary health centers
options.C: Bridging the gap between formal health facilities and grassroots populations
options.D: Enforcing strict national prison sentences for people who eat junk food

explanation: Spot on! Community nurses take health education, screenings, and support right to the doorsteps and neighborhoods where people live. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h6)

question: If an older child or teenager faints right after getting an injection, what is this usually classified as?

options.A: Immunization anxiety-related reaction
options.B: Coincidental infection process
options.C: Product-related systemic reaction
options.D: Vaccine quality defect-related reaction

explanation: Needle fear is real! Fainting right after a shot is typically an anxiety-related reaction, not a bad reaction to the vaccine itself. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h5)

question: A nurse accidentally pricks her finger with a hollow needle used to draw blood. What is the biggest worry?

options.A: Suffering from severe immediate muscle spasms
options.B: Developing an acute allergic reaction to latex
options.C: Developing localized skin necrosis on the finger
options.D: Exposure to bloodborne pathogens like HIV and Hepatitis

explanation: Hollow needles often hold infected blood inside them, which is why a prick poses a direct threat of viral transmission. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which viral infection is known as the main cause of cervical cancer?

options.A: Hepatitis B Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Herpes Simplex Virus

explanation: Yes! High-risk strains of HPV are strongly linked to almost all cervical cancer cases. Keeping safe is key! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h3)

question: What happens when a nurse falls into 'confirmation bias' during clinical assessment?

options.A: Forgetting to check vital signs because of a sudden emergency
options.B: Trusting equipment alarms even when they are making false noises
options.C: Blaming a coworker for a mistake you made during a procedure
options.D: Looking only for signs that prove your first guess and ignoring others

explanation: You got it! Confirmation bias is when our brain only looks for clues that match our very first thought about what is wrong, while ignoring other important signs. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h2)

question: Where does peripheral fatigue mainly start in the body?

options.A: Along the main pathways of the spinal cord
options.B: Inside the cerebral cortex of the brain
options.C: Within the muscle fibers or neuromuscular junction
options.D: Through systemic inflammatory cytokines in the blood

explanation: You've got this! Peripheral fatigue happens right at the muscles and the junctions where nerves meet them. Even though your brain sends the signal to move, the muscles themselves are just too worn out to respond properly. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T3#GNS123_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the main cause of spreading infections through unsafe injections?

options.A: Reusing single-use syringes without proper sterilization
options.B: Using the wrong size needle for subcutaneous injections
options.C: Administering expired medications into the muscle

question: What is the main difference between an 'adolescent' and 'adolescence'?

question: Why should you call or alert the receiving hospital before the patient physically arrives?

question: Why do we bother doing nursing research in the first place?

question: Why can slouching lead to tummy troubles like heartburn or constipation?

question: Why is a standard serving size for dried fruit much smaller than fresh fruit?

question: Why should nurses be quick to spot the difference between side effects and true adverse drug reactions?

question: A public hospital lacks funds to buy a new CT scanner and partners with a private firm to supply and run it. What is the key benefit here?

question: Why is a suspected hole (perforation) in the gut a major warning sign against using regular barium?

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

question: How should nurses and doctors communicate with a family after an adverse event?

question: Which phase of a rescue operation involves sweeping the disaster area to find where victims are trapped?

question: Why do lecturers love using concept maps and breaking long topics into smaller pieces?

question: What is a main duty of an occupational health nurse working as a case manager?

question: A patient presents with irregular periods, excess facial hair, and trouble conceiving due to missing ovulation. Which condition does this suggest?

question: What is a common negative impact of social stigma on patients managing HIV?

question: Why do we say communication is a clinical intervention, just like giving medicine?

question: Why is it important to involve traditional leaders and local birth attendants in primary health care?

question: Why does a patient moving around during a digital blood pressure check often cause an error?

question: Why do some patients with gallbladder disease develop jaundice (yellow skin)?

question: Why is it super important to check the publication date of an article before using it for clinical care?

question: A mother brings her young child with sickle cell anaemia to the clinic. Which statement by the mother shows she understands home care instructions?

question: An elderly patient with less muscle and more body fat takes a water-soluble drug. What is the likely result?

question: Which important hormone does the placenta make to keep early pregnancy going strong?

question: What role do continuing professional development programs play in nursing?

options.A: Historical research
options.B: Qualitative research
options.C: Quantitative research
options.D: Biographical research

question: What is the primary function of cerebrospinal fluid?

options.A: To transmit electrical signals across synapses
options.B: To cushion the brain and provide nutritional support
options.C: To produce red blood cells for nervous tissue
options.D: To cool down the body during a high fever

explanation: CSF acts as a shock-absorbing liquid cushion while also nourishing the central nervous system tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h7)

question: What are the standard cardinal signs evaluated during a routine physical assessment?

options.A: Temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure
options.B: Pain level, reflex response, pupil size, and skin color
options.C: Mental status, urine output, bowel sounds, and core temperature
options.D: Weight, height, blood glucose, and visual acuity

explanation: The four classic cardinal vital signs reflect the most critical life-sustaining physiological functions of the body. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which of these best describes emotional abuse?

options.A: Withholding financial resources to pay for basic food items
options.B: Constant insults and public humiliation intended to destroy self-esteem
options.C: Denying access to emergency medical care during an illness
options.D: The intentional use of physical force to cause bodily injury

explanation: Great job! Emotional abuse hits a person's mental peace through constant insults, shaming, and public humiliation to break down their confidence. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T10#GNS312_U4_T10_h3)

question: You accidentally give a patient twice the right dose of their blood pressure medication. What is your very first step?

options.A: Blame the pharmacy assistant for supplying the wrong concentration of tablets.
options.B: Quietly monitor the patient from afar so no one finds out about the mistake.
options.C: Leave the shift early so you are not around when the patient's blood pressure drops.
options.D: Assess the patient's vital signs, notify the doctor, and document the event factually.

explanation: Brave and correct! Patient safety always comes first. Check on your patient, call the doctor immediately, and be honest in your reporting. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why do human-made disasters often catch us off guard and create complex challenges?

options.A: They only affect critical infrastructure and leave human populations unharmed
options.B: They strike suddenly without warning and leave behind persistent secondary dangers
options.C: They are easily contained and never require outside medical assistance
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of subsequent environmental contamination

explanation: Great thinking! Because these events happen without warning and leave behind things like toxic smoke or weak buildings, they keep emergency responders on high alert. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h1)

question: As a psychiatric nurse evaluating a patient's unusual symptom, what is the most important question to ask yourself?

options.A: How quickly can medication completely erase this behavior?
options.B: What is the exact medical billing code for this diagnosis?
options.C: Which family member caused the patient to act this way?
options.D: What purpose does this symptom serve for the patient?

explanation: Always look for the 'why.' Understanding what job the symptom is doing for the patient helps you uncover its protective or adaptive role. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to teamwork across sectors in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive funding and immediate budget releases for all health programs
options.B: Sectoral sidelining and agencies operating in isolation
options.C: Bureaucratic red tape between different government tiers
options.D: Frequent changes in local political leadership

explanation: You got it! Chronic underfunding and delayed budgets are huge hurdles—we definitely don't have the problem of 'too much money'! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h6)

question: Which specific antidote is given for a paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Activated charcoal
options.B: Protamine sulfate
options.C: Naloxone hydrochloride
options.D: N-acetylcysteine

explanation: N-acetylcysteine (often called NAC) is the lifesaving go-to for paracetamol overdoses. It restores liver protectors (glutathione) just in time to save the liver cells. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h3)

question: A 14-year-old girl is growing fast and has started her monthly periods. How does this affect her food and nutrient needs?

options.A: She only needs extra water and no other dietary changes
options.B: Her nutritional demands decrease because her body is slowing down
options.C: Her nutritional demands remain exactly the same as childhood
options.D: Her nutritional demands increase significantly to support growth and blood loss

question: Why do doctors and nurses sometimes give patients two or more medications at the same time?

options.A: To achieve a better therapeutic advantage for the patient
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing separate prescriptions
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for patient monitoring
options.D: To speed up the physical breakdown of tablets in the stomach

explanation: Great question! Sometimes teamwork makes the dream work—combining meds (like for high blood pressure) helps control an illness much better than using just one drug alone. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why does a strict blame culture hurt patient safety over time?

options.A: It makes staff hide mistakes and close calls out of fear
options.B: It places too much financial burden on the hospital administration
options.C: It makes nurses calculate medications by hand more often
options.D: It stops nurses from getting proper clinical certifications

explanation: When punishment is guaranteed, nurses stay quiet. We need open communication to fix dangerous processes together! [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h1)
